learning: Iteration 3 (wheel_track 0.09, 12 mm sensors) gave 448.7, with the oval at 20 of 20 but slalom line losses rising to 1.85. Iteration 4 tests a 16 mm footprint with the controller held fixed. If slalom losses recover but the s-bend stays at the floor, the limit is likely controller gain or turn authority rather than geometry.
notes: Iteration 4 package: sensor_size 0.016 with all other geometry from iteration 3, and the iteration 3 controller held fixed to isolate the footprint change. Based on iteration 3's slalom losses of 1.85 and s-bend max_error at the 0.06 floor.
rationale: Iteration 3 (score 448.7) is the best raced design. Its oval finishes 20 of 20 with max_error 0.025, and the s-bend still goes off track in 18 of 20 trials at progress 0.68, with line_loss_events 1.0, max_error at the 0.06 m floor (0.0607) and steering_oscillation 0.32. Slalom line losses are 1.85 with progress 0.17, up from 1.0 at iteration 2, so the 12 mm footprint is too narrow for the alternating bends. The Builder's proposal changes only sensor_size from 0.012 to 0.016, which is the lever the slalom and s-bend triggers pointed to. I accept that geometry unchanged. At 15 mm pitch on a 25 mm tape with a centred line, the readings should be about [0, 0.34, 1, 0.34, 0]. The weights stay antisymmetric and give a zero signal when centred, and the outer sensors still see nothing until the robot is well off centre. Because the Builder asked to isolate the footprint, I keep the iteration 3 controller exactly (kp 2.8, ki 0.05, kd 0.5, base_speed 1.5, last_direction). That keeps the cause of any change attributable to sensor_size alone. The main risk is that the blurrier edge signal lowers the signal slope and adds lag or jitter on the s-bend. The observation request covers per-track line losses, max_error and oscillation so that case can be seen. Expected, not measured: slalom line losses back near 1.0, s-bend line losses below 1.0 and s-bend max_error below 0.06 on some seeds, with the oval still at 20 of 20.
